<div class="theme-admonition theme-admonition-note admonition_joKL alert alert--secondary"><div class="admonitionHeading_lJJ_"><span class="admonitionIcon_nSNi"><svg viewBox="0 0 14 16"><path fill-rule="evenodd" d="M6.3 5.69a.942.942 0 0 1-.28-.7c0-.28.09-.52.28-.7.19-.18.42-.28.7-.28.28 0 .52.09.7.28.18.19.28.42.28.7 0 .28-.09.52-.28.7a1 1 0 0 1-.7.3c-.28 0-.52-.11-.7-.3zM8 7.99c-.02-.25-.11-.48-.31-.69-.2-.19-.42-.3-.69-.31H6c-.27.02-.48.13-.69.31-.2.2-.3.44-.31.69h1v3c.02.27.11.5.31.69.2.2.42.31.69.31h1c.27 0 .48-.11.69-.31.2-.19.3-.42.31-.69H8V7.98v.01zM7 2.3c-3.14 0-5.7 2.54-5.7 5.68 0 3.14 2.56 5.7 5.7 5.7s5.7-2.55 5.7-5.7c0-3.15-2.56-5.69-5.7-5.69v.01zM7 .98c3.86 0 7 3.14 7 7s-3.14 7-7 7-7-3.12-7-7 3.14-7 7-7z"></path></svg></span>note</div><div class="admonitionContent_yU2W"><p><strong>Note:</strong> Only clients listed in the <a href="https://www.figma.com/mcp-catalog/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Figma MCP Catalog</a> like VS Code, Cursor, or Claude Code can connect to the Figma MCP Server. If you're a developer interested in connecting a new MCP client, you can <a href="https://form.asana.com/?k=kBG-ejRQTdY8x_H6a4vM3Q&d=10497086658021" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">join the waitlist</a>.</p></div></div>
<p>The Figma MCP server brings Figma directly into your workflow by providing important design information and context to AI agents generating code from Figma design files.</p>
<p>MCP servers are part of a standardized interface for AI agents to interact with data sources using the <a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Model Context Protocol</a>.</p>
<p>Figma's remote MCP server makes it possible to connect directly to your Figma files without needing to install Figma's desktop app. You can capture live UI to Figma Design and bring design context into your workflow wherever you're working.</p>
<p>With the server enabled, you can:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Write to canvas</strong>: Use a supported MCP client to create and modify native Figma content directly in Figma Design and FigJam files. Agents can build and update frames, components, variables, and auto layout in Design files, or create and edit FigJam boards using stickies, sections, connectors, and shapes.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Generate designs from live UI</strong>: Use a supported MCP client to capture the live UI of your web app or site and send it to new and existing Figma files or your clipboard. (<a href="/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/">select clients only</a>)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Generate code from selected frames</strong>: Select a Figma frame and turn it into code. Great for product teams building new flows or iterating on app features.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Generate diagrams in FigJam</strong>: Create architecture diagrams and ERDs from prompts, code, or structured inputs. Diagrams can be generated in a new FigJam file or added to an existing one.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Extract design context</strong>: Pull in variables, components, and layout data directly into your IDE. This is especially useful for design systems and component-based workflows.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Retrieve Make resources</strong>: <a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/bringing-make-context-to-your-agent/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Gather code resources from Make files</a> and provide them to the LLM as context. This can help as you move from prototype to production application.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Keep your design system components consistent with Code Connect</strong>: Boost output quality by reusing your actual components. Code Connect keeps your generated code consistent with your codebase.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>To use this server, you'll need to sign in through Figma's OAuth authentication flow. Once set up, the remote server gives you a seamless way to access Figma data and integrate it with your tools.</p>

<h4 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="using-the-figma-plugin-for-xcode-preferred">Using the Figma plugin for Xcode (preferred):<a href="#using-the-figma-plugin-for-xcode-preferred" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Using the Figma plugin for Xcode (preferred):" title="Direct link to Using the Figma plugin for Xcode (preferred):" translate="no">​</a></h4>
<p>The recommended way to set up the Figma MCP server in Xcode is by installing the Figma plugin, which includes MCP server settings as well as Agent Skills for common workflows.</p>
<p>To install the Figma plugin, use Xcode's one-click setup and authorize the MCP server for your Figma account: <a href="xcode://agent-plugin-clone?repo=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Ffigma%2Fmcp-server-guide" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">One-click setup</a></p>
<p>To confirm the plugin is installed, go to <strong>Settings</strong> in Xcode, then click <strong>Intelligence</strong>. The Figma plugin will be listed in the <strong>Plug-ins</strong> section.</p>
<h4 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="manual-setup-for-xcode">Manual setup for Xcode:<a href="#manual-setup-for-xcode" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Manual setup for Xcode:" title="Direct link to Manual setup for Xcode:" translate="no">​</a></h4>
<p>If you prefer, you can manually set up the remote Figma MCP server. There's no difference in functionality if you follow the manual steps.</p>
<p>In Xcode:</p>
<ol>
<li>Go to <strong>Settings</strong>, and then click <strong>Intelligence</strong>.</li>
<li>Install an agent such as Claude Agent, Codex, or Gemini.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Plug-ins</strong>.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Add plug-in</strong>.</li>
<li>Choose <strong>Add from URL</strong>.</li>
<li>Enter the following in the URL field: <a href="https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><code>https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide</code></a></li>
<li>Choose the <strong>Figma Plug-in</strong>.</li>
<li>Once added, authorize your Figma account to use the MCP server in Xcode.</li>
</ol>
<h2 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="using-the-mcp-server">Using the MCP server<a href="#using-the-mcp-server" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Using the MCP server" title="Direct link to Using the MCP server" translate="no">​</a></h2>
<p>The MCP server introduces a set of tools that help LLMs bring your live UI to Figma Design and get design context from Figma. Once connected, you can start prompting your MCP client.</p>
<p>For a complete list of tools and examples, see <a href="/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/">Tools and Prompts</a>.</p>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="example-send-ui-to-figma">Example: Send UI to Figma<a href="#example-send-ui-to-figma" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Example: Send UI to Figma" title="Direct link to Example: Send UI to Figma" translate="no">​</a></h3>

See <a href="/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/">Code to canvas</a>.</p></div></div>
<p>Sending the live UI of your web app or site to Figma is done through conversation with your MCP client:</p>
<ol>
<li>Prompt your MCP client: "Start a local server for my app and capture the UI in a new Figma file.”</li>
<li>Follow the steps your client provides. Your client will open a browser window for you, or give you a link to follow.</li>
<li>Use the capture toolbar to capture pages, elements, and states of your web app or site.</li>
<li>Let your client know when you're finished. Your client will give you a link to open the Figma file that was created.</li>
</ol>
